description: We are CS/CE RWTH students who are interested in cosmic horror
summary:
NASA's fire record goes back to 2000, but the same satellites didn't collect all of it. MODIS on Terra and Aqua came first. From 2012 the VIIRS sensors joined: Suomi NPP, NOAA-20 in 2018 and NOAA-21 in 2023. VIIRS picks up much smaller fires, so each new satellite pushed the raw detection counts up, even where nothing changed on the ground. In our La Rioja box in Argentina, raw yearly detections went from 868 in 2011 to 3,437 in 2012.

We took 7.08 million FIRMS detections and gave every VIIRS detection a weight, so the totals can be read as MODIS-equivalent counts. The weights were fitted on Argentina 2012–2021. On 2022–2024, which the method never saw, the bias dropped from +786% for raw VIIRS to +6.7%, with R² 0.79 per cell and month. It also held on NOAA-21, which wasn't in the training data (R² 0.93).

FireWatch shows the result as one month-by-year calendar for 26 years, raw or harmonized. In April 2011, 17 MODIS detections on the Belgian side of the Hohes Venn look about 6 times normal in the raw data. After harmonization the same month is about 29 times normal, the highest April in 26 years.

These are satellite detections, not confirmed fires, and the transfer to Europe is weaker for large events
details:
FireWatch is a calendar of NASA FIRMS active fire detections from 2000 to 2026. Pick a region and you get a month-by-year heatmap, a map, annual totals and a 30-day outlook.

The satellite record is not consistent: MODIS has observed since 2000, and the more sensitive VIIRS satellites joined in 2012, 2018 and 2023. Each one makes the raw count jump. In La Rioja, Argentina, detections went from 868 in 2011 to 3,437 in 2012 with no real change on the ground.

We convert VIIRS detections into MODIS units using ratios measured in Argentina for 2012–2021. The La Rioja step becomes 868 → 808. On 2022–2024, which we kept out of training, the result matches MODIS with R² = 0.79.

A detection is a hot pixel, not a confirmed fire, and the converted number is an estimate that runs high in large events.

Built with Python, pandas, Streamlit, Folium and Plotly on NASA FIRMS data.
dataRefs: NASA FIRMS (Fire Information for Resource Management System))
